chief_complaint: profound sadness, loss of interest in hobbies, and terminal insomnia for 3 months
hpi_details: 38M librarian presents with 3 months of persistent low mood, loss of interest in reading and piano (anhedonia), early morning awakening at 3 AM, and constant fatigue. Reports feelings of worthlessness.
ideas: thinks he is a failure and has lost his spark
concerns: worried he will never feel happy again
expectations: wants medication to lift the dark mood

clinical_knowledge.topic: Major Depressive Disorder evaluation and management
core_concepts: Major depressive disorder requires a depressive episode with clinically significant distress or impairment, after excluding bipolar disorder, substance-related causes, and relevant medical conditions.
Assess severity, psychotic symptoms, functional decline, suicide risk, access to means, protective factors, and capacity for a collaborative safety plan.
Screen carefully for past mania or hypomania before antidepressant treatment.
Psychotherapy and/or an antidepressant may be appropriate after shared decision-making; selection, dose, and monitoring must be individualized.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: profound sadness, loss of interest in hobbies, and terminal insomnia for 3 months

Key HPI features: 38M librarian presents with 3 months of persistent low mood, loss of interest in reading and piano (anhedonia), early morning awakening at 3 AM, and constant fatigue. Reports feelings of worthlessness.
Objective/Exam findings: Mental-state examination, suicide-risk assessment, and targeted physical examination or tests when history suggests a medical contributor.
Relevant background/PMH: No prior psychiatric history
common_misconceptions: Prescribing an antidepressant before screening for mania or hypomania.
Using a screening score alone to determine diagnosis or immediate risk.
Assuming absence of volunteered suicidal thoughts means risk is absent.
dangerous_errors: Failing to urgently assess active suicidal intent, a plan, access to lethal means, recent attempt, psychosis, severe self-neglect, or inability to stay safe.
Starting an antidepressant without discussing adverse effects, early activation, interactions, bipolar risk, and follow-up.
management_principles: Complete a diagnostic, mental-state, and suicide-risk assessment, including bipolar screening.
Offer evidence-based psychotherapy and discuss antidepressant treatment when indicated using shared decision-making and planned monitoring.
Create a collaborative safety plan and restrict access to lethal means where appropriate; arrange urgent emergency assessment if safety cannot be maintained.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Persistent depressed mood and pervasive anhedonia lasting at least two weeks, severely impairing daily psychosocial functioning.

must_ask.objective: Mood and anhedonia specific to lost hobbies
must_ask.say: Have you lost interest in reading or playing piano, things you used to enjoy?
Are you waking up very early in the morning and unable to fall back asleep?
Do you feel constantly fatigued, or like you're not good enough?
Have you had any thoughts of ending your life?

must_ask.objective: Prior manic or hypomanic episode screening
must_ask.say: Have you ever had a period of unusually elevated mood or energy?

history.answer: For the past three months, I've felt overwhelmingly sad and empty, and I just can't bring myself to do anything anymore.
It started about three months ago and has been present almost every single day, from the moment I wake up until night.
There was no specific event or loss that triggered this; work and life were normal, but this dark feeling just crept in.
I used to love playing the piano and reading literature every evening, but I haven't felt any joy in them and haven't touched either in months.
I fall asleep around eleven without trouble, but I wake up suddenly at 3 AM every morning and lie awake feeling miserable until dawn.
I have had almost no appetite lately and have to force myself to eat, losing about four kilograms over the past three months.
I feel completely drained and exhausted all day long, even when I spend the whole weekend resting.
My concentration at the library is terrible; cataloging books takes me twice as long, and even simple decisions overwhelm me.
I constantly feel like a complete failure to everyone around me and that I'm just useless and taking up space.
People at work told me I walk and speak much slower now, and my arms and legs feel heavy like lead.
When I wake up alone at 3 AM, the thought crosses my mind that it might be easier if I just didn't wake up, but I have no desire to hurt myself.
No, I do not have any plan or means to end my life, and I have never attempted suicide.
My parents and my sister mean the world to me, and I could never put them through that pain.
It has become very hard to keep up with my duties at the library, and I have stopped seeing friends or leaving home on weekends.
No, I have never experienced a period of feeling unusually energetic, euphoric, or needing little sleep.
No, I have never heard voices or seen things that other people cannot, and I have no strange or paranoid beliefs.
I do not drink alcohol, and I have never used sleeping pills, cannabis, or recreational drugs.
No, I haven't noticed sensitivity to cold, constipation, swelling in my neck, or dry skin.
No, this is the very first time in my life that I have ever felt depressed or experienced anything like this.
I keep thinking that I have lost my spark and that I am failing at my life and career.
I am terrified that this heavy darkness will never lift and that I will never be able to feel happy again.
I am really hoping you might be able to prescribe some medication to help lift this dark cloud.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid disease.
I have never undergone any surgery and have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or nutritional supplements.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I work as a librarian at a municipal library and live alone in an apartment.
No one in my family has ever been diagnosed with depression, bipolar disorder, or died by suicide.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Clean attire with slumped posture, subdued facial expression, decreased eye contact, and noticeably reduced spontaneous motor movement.

Alert and fully oriented to person, place, and time; speech is soft and slow; reported mood is profoundly depressed with flat-to-constricted affect; thought process is linear with no active suicidal intent or psychotic features; insight and judgment are preserved.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, symmetrical, without palpable nodules or bruits.
Conjunctivae are pink and non-pale; sclerae are clear and non-icteric.
Skin has normal texture and turgor, with no dryness, coarseness, myxedema, or rashes.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric at the biceps, patella, and Achilles tendons, with normal relaxation phases bilaterally.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal first and second heart sounds, no audible murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with no crackles, wheezes, or decreased breath sounds.
